# The larger of two magnitudes, and the and of two masks

Kernel `norm_combine` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The larger of $m$ and $n$, exactly, by a comparison; and the mask $\mathit{okr}$ of a fold of maxima, true while no element was a NaN, which the claims do not describe:

$$r = \max(m, n).$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of [`norm_step_1`](norm_step_1.md). It is part of the loop `bv_make_1`, called by the constructors of `BallVector<T, 1, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 1>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)); and of the loop `bv_make_2_entry`, called by the constructors of `BallVector<T, 2, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 2>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)); and of the loop `bv_neg_1`, called by `-x` and `neg(x, z)` of `BallVector<T, 1, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 1>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)); and of the loop `bv_neg_2`, called by `-x` and `neg(x, z)` of `BallVector<T, 2, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 2>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)); and of the loop `bv_add_1`, called by `x + y`, `x += y`, `add(x, y, z)` and `axpy` of `BallVector<T, 1, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 1>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)); and of the loop `bv_add_2`, called by `x + y`, `x += y`, `add(x, y, z)` and `axpy` of `BallVector<T, 2, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 2>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)); and of the loop `bv_sub_1`, called by `x - y`, `x -= y` and `sub(x, y, z)` of `BallVector<T, 1, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 1>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)); and of the loop `bv_sub_2`, called by `x - y`, `x -= y` and `sub(x, y, z)` of `BallVector<T, 2, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 2>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)); ## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $r = \max(m, n)$, exactly: the larger of the two.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `norm_combine_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/FoldNorm.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/FoldNorm.v), against `norm_combine_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions norm_combine_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition norm_combine_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall m n : R,
  forall ok okn : bool,
  fmt emin prec m ->
  fmt emin prec n ->
  let '(r, okr) := norm_combine m ok n okn in
  fmt emin prec r /\
  r = Rmax m n.
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `norm_combine_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the larger of two numbers, by a comparison (milestone2.md, norm_upper_k). **License:** proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/norm_combine.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/norm_combine.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The combination of the folds of maxima norm_upper_k (milestone2.md, "sum, dot, axpy,
# convolution": norm_upper_k; architecture.md, "Folds of maxima"): the larger of two magnitudes,
# and the and of two masks, each true when no element folded into its state was a NaN. A maximum
# computed by a comparison keeps m when n is a NaN (lt is false): the steps keep such a NaN in the
# mask instead (norm_step_1). On every pair of states it is a maximum and an and, which are
# associative, commutative and idempotent: the result of the fold does not depend on the order.

c   = lt(m, n)
r   = select(c, n, m)
okr = and(ok, okn)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 2**: the runs of commit `5f597fb`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#norm_combine)).

**These runs judged other claims.** They judged `maximum(r) of m, n`; the kernel now claims `maximum(r)`. Their numbers are not about the statement above.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 584 180 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
